quote: Es wird übrigens der Nachweis wohl doch leichter sein, als ich denke.
english: Incidentally, the proof will probably be easier after all than I think.
topic: The page discusses how hard it is to prove that a differential equation cannot be solved by a single quadrature, then asks how solids, liquids, gases, aether and electricity should be described under molecular theory using mean values and expansions in small parameters, and finally states that the function zeta(s,x) = sum x^n/n^s satisfies no known differential equation.

triage.modern_statement: The sentence follows Hilbert's remark that it is hard to prove that a given differential equation cannot be solved by a single quadrature. In modern terms that is a non-integrability statement: the solutions do not lie in an extension of the base differential field obtained by adjoining one integral, a question studied in differential Galois theory (Picard–Vessiot). The summary does not name the equation, so the exact claim cannot be pinned down. One other reading is possible: the 'proof' could be the page's last claim, that Li_s(x) = ζ(s,x) = Σ x^n/n^s satisfies no algebraic (partial) differential equation in s and x. Hilbert published that claim in his 1900 Paris address.
triage.answered_by: The quadrature claim cannot be identified because the equation is not named. If the sentence means the ζ(s,x) claim, that was proved by A. Ostrowski in 'Über Dirichletsche Reihen und algebraische Differentialgleichungen' (Math. Z., 1920). The one-variable case, that the Riemann ζ(s) satisfies no algebraic ODE, was proved by Stadigh and by Mordukhai-Boltovskoi, and also by Ostrowski.

evidence.claim: In his 1900 problem list, just after the 18th problem, Hilbert said that ζ(s,x) = Σ x^n/n^s, which is closely related to ζ(s), probably satisfies no algebraic partial differential equation. Ostrowski justified this in 1920.

Ostrowski's 1920 thesis-era result proved that the Dirichlet zeta series ζ(x,s) satisfies no algebraic partial differential equation, which partly answered Hilbert's 18th problem as his biographers put it.
There is an English translation of Ostrowski's 'On Dirichlet Series and Algebraic Differential Equations'.
Hilbert's 1900 statement that ζ(s) satisfies no algebraic differential equation was proved independently by Mordukhai-Boltovskoi and by Ostrowski.
In the published address, Hilbert derives the result for ζ(s) from Hölder's theorem on Γ(x) together with the functional equation.

triage.why: From the page order, 'the proof will be easier than I think' most likely refers to the just-mentioned impossibility of solving some differential equation by a single quadrature. The page summary does not say which equation, so I cannot identify a precise problem or trace its fate. If Hilbert instead meant the differential transcendence of ζ(s,x), then the claim is well known: it went into the 1900 address as a remark next to Problem 18, not as one of the numbered 23 problems, and Ostrowski proved it in 1920. Work on differential independence of ζ and Γ continues today, but that does not confirm that this diary note is about ζ.
